text:
The model sees almost nothing separating the Islanders and Senators tonight in Ottawa, projecting 2.75 expected goals for OTT and 2.68 for NYI. The underlying numbers explain why. Ottawa has been the steadier defensive team, allowing 2.96 expected goals per 60 minutes to New York's 3.52, while the Islanders create slightly more at 2.94 to 2.83. New York's results have run ahead of its process: it has allowed just 2.5 goals a game despite those chance totals, while Ottawa's 2.86 scored and 2.71 allowed look about right. On special teams, both power plays generate 0.74 expected goals per game, but Ottawa's penalty kill (0.75 against) is far tighter than New York's (1.08). The Senators also draw 5.86 penalties a game, so that gap could matter.

The goalie matchup favors a pair of hot starters. Projected starter Ilya Sorokin has saved 6.16 goals above expected in five games (.930), and Linus Ullmark, also projected, sits at 6.77 (.950) over five. Last season they pointed in opposite directions: Sorokin was 22.3 goals above expected over 55 games, while Ullmark was 13.3 below over 49. This is the first meeting between the teams this season.

Form is mixed on both sides. Ottawa's last five games brought two regulation wins, a shootout win and two losses, including a 7-2 loss to STL on Tuesday in which it held only 34 percent of the expected goals. New York won three of its last five and has scored 6-0 and 4-1 wins, though the 5-2 and 5-3 losses leaked goals. For individual picks, the model likes Tim Stützle to score at 32 percent and to reach two points at 28 percent, with Drake Batherson at 28 percent to score. For New York, Bo Horvat leads at 33 percent to score and 21 percent for two points, with Matthew Schaefer at 17 percent for two points.
